To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the population of European hamsters inhabiting the urban area is characterized by a lower species diversity and number of predators, and a higher preying pressure of unattended feral dogs and cats.

the hamsters in the area with a higher level and different kind human activity have been adapted to urban environment by adjustment of their activity to the rhythm of the human activity and slightly increased caution, shown in higher locomotor activity, while their population density is similar to that in rural areas.

the population of hamsters in the periurban area has a higher number of burrows, a higher number of individuals, a lower number of predators, a lower species diversity of predators and a higher preying pressure of cats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the hamsters living in the periurban areas can be considered as an example of a population adapted to human activity.
the possibility of using urban areas for the development of hamsters population.
the possibility of hamsters’ adaptation to living in the urbanized areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hamster populations in periurban and rural localities differ in their functioning, but in both cases they are able to function in human-modified habitats.
the urbanization of rural areas does not lead to a complete loss of hamsters, but it does not contribute to the improvement of its conservation.
the periurban areas are a more favourable habitat for the hamster population than rural areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the urbanization and development of infrastructure are the main factors that determine the functioning and dynamics of hamsters populations.
hamsters living in the vicinity of the urbanized area are able to adapt to the presence of man.
the periurban area is a suitable habitat for hamsters and the species can live in the vicinity of humans without problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hamsters living near the urbanized areas have a higher chance of survival than those inhabiting the rural areas.
the urbanization and human presence can have both positive and negative influence on the functioning of the local population.
hamsters are able to adapt to urban areas and they can be a good example for other species of wild animals to adapt to urban conditions.
